proposition: Without ranking from filenames, what do inventoried permit documents establish, and which document governs if they disagree?
would_establish: Issued final_permit cover pages authorize discharge only under named internal parts (Parts I–III/IV and cross-referenced appendices), defining the governing authorization corpus without using filename kind as hierarchy.
Part II appendix and Part IV inventoried files are incorporated into the issued final_permit by internal cross-reference rather than standing as independent authorization documents.
Fact sheets and statements of basis frame content as draft/proposed rationale or administrative record and defer enforceable limitations to the issued or draft permit.
Reasonable-potential files are calculation workbooks subordinate to fact sheets, not standalone authorization documents.
document_inventory.json document_kind labels alone do not determine conflict precedence; document text must govern classification and authority.
would_refute: Filename or inventory document_kind values (final_permit > fact_sheet > reasonable_potential, etc.) determine both content authority and conflict precedence.
All twelve inventoried files are independently binding with no functional precedence among them.
Precedence is entirely unknowable unless an explicit 'in the event of conflict' clause appears between package documents.
insufficient_alone: sources/document_inventory.json provides path, permit, document_kind, and hash but no precedence or incorporation metadata beyond kind labels.
documents/INDEX.md lists filenames and kinds but contains no narrative authority rules.
A single final_permit cover page establishes self-definition for that permit only; it does not by itself resolve minor_modification authority for NM0000116.
PRIOR_PACKET.json is bounded prior retrieval, not authoritative disposition.
